scope: Independent full-viewport visual review of the ten frozen round-2 iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 Simulator screenshots. Sessions and People retrieval only; synthetic workspace.
score_kind: Subjective visual craft judgment; not a behavioral score or a measurement of human preference.

category_breakdown.assessment: Topics and names lead at regular size. Review attention stays visibly separate from the read/unread surface treatment. At AX5 the fixed utility header and composer retain considerable visual and viewport priority over retrieval content.

The reviewed identity, topic, context and time strings remain legible. Type uses weight, size and tone coherently, including Chinese dark mode. AX5 content wraps and continues through scrolling; the supplied subsequent viewports are not evidence of export clipping. No meaningful typography-only defect was identified in this bounded content sample.

Regular rows have stable text baselines and comfortable grouping, and sparse results remain honestly sparse. The AX5 People composition retains an accessory-only row and a separator inset that no longer follows the full-width text column.

Warm surfaces, restrained separators and the selective unread card are coherent. The persistent light composer has unusually prominent elevation for this quiet retrieval surface, and the AX5 dotted attention icon becomes a large decorative companion to an already explicit text label.

Sessions and People share page selection, search/filter controls, count treatment and menus. The visible active filter and its remove command are clear. Light, dark and AX5 retain the same retrieval identity, with one visible Chinese-locale label inconsistency.

deductions.observation: At AX5 the result count and Synthetic preview consume two fixed lines above the list, while the bottom Ask anything composer stays fully expanded. This same shelf remains in both subsequent scroll captures. The individual labels appear short enough for a width-fitting shared line in this exact sample.
deductions.judgment: A residual full-viewport hierarchy issue: low-priority disclosure and shell support reduce how much identity/context can be read together. Scrolling or large text itself is not the defect, and no content-access failure is inferred.

deductions.observation: The small initials avatar and menu sit in a separate accessory-only row above the very large name. In 08, this produces a weakly occupied horizontal band before Leila; 10 also exposes the next avatar/menu band before the next person's text.
deductions.judgment: The AX5 row has an avoidable interruption in identity grouping. The viewport boundary in 10 is normal scrolling and is not counted as clipping or inaccessible content.

deductions.observation: The regular People separator starts at the inset name column. In 10, the AX5 name/context/time have moved to the row's full-width leading edge, but the separator still begins substantially to their right.
deductions.judgment: The old avatar-column inset survives after the row changes composition, weakening alignment between the text block and its closing rule.

deductions.observation: The full-width pale composer has a bright outline and broad shadow, giving it more persistent elevation than the mostly flat retrieval content.
deductions.judgment: This is a minor material preference grounded in the rubric's scarce-elevation criterion: the command is useful, but its surrounding visual mass is stronger than necessary.

deductions.observation: The compact dotted Review needed symbol in 01 expands into a large dotted ring in 09 beside a two-line red Review needed label.
deductions.judgment: The explicit readable label already carries the state. The much larger ring adds visual urgency and lateral weight without adding meaning; this is not a request to reduce the user's text size.

deductions.observation: Candidate remains English in both People rows beside localized navigation, result count and 2周前 recency.
deductions.judgment: The visible person-kind label is inconsistent with the Chinese shell. English names, employers and search titles are treated as workspace content and are not penalized. Confirm the label's ownership before changing it.

corrections.correction: Refine the fixed retrieval utility shelf at AX5: let count and Synthetic preview share a line when their actual rendered widths fit, preserve the disclosure and all commands, and reduce the composer's surrounding shadow.
corrections.verification: Recapture the same four AX5 states and regular light pages. Verify unchanged readable text sizes, full disclosure, 44-point command targets and retrieval access, with less utility height/elevation.

corrections.correction: Recompose AX5 row accessories around the text: group the People avatar/menu with the name, align the separator to the active text column, and keep the Review needed symbol visually subordinate to its full-size label.
corrections.verification: Compare 08–10 equivalents at AX5. The name and menu must remain accessible, the first menu must still be hittable and at least 44 by 44 points, separators must follow the text column, and review attention must retain its readable non-color label.

corrections.correction: If Candidate is the app-owned person-kind label, localize it in the Chinese People surface without translating stored names, employers or search titles.
corrections.verification: Recapture Chinese People and confirm consistent app labels with unchanged synthetic identity and context content.

behavioral_evidence_boundary: The frozen input reports three focused policy tests, eight native UI checks, final anchor restoration checks, first-person AX5 menu hittability and 44-point geometry, CUA readback, and token-derived contrast checks. Those are supporting reported evidence, not tests personally executed or raw result bundles inspected by this reviewer. Still images establish visible composition only.

functional_gates.search_filter_reset: Reported exercised in tests-r2.xcresult; 04 visibly shows active scope and removal affordance. Runtime behavior is not independently verified here.
functional_gates.read_unread: 01/02/05 visibly distinguish read/unread surfaces from review attention; semantics and handlers are reported exercised, not directly tested here.
functional_gates.command_targets: The first People AX5 menu is reported verified at least 44 by 44 points and hittable. Complete command-target geometry is not independently inspected.
functional_gates.page_navigation_and_content_access: Visible page selection and subsequent AX5 scroll positions support coherence; the input reports native/CUA navigation and access checks. No direct interaction was performed.
functional_gates.identity_provenance_and_external_writes: The input states these semantics were not intentionally changed and retrieval performs no external action. This review does not independently audit persistence, provenance integrity or absence of writes.

missing_evidence: Direct VoiceOver order, focus, names and action inspection; static menu glyphs and reported CUA labels do not establish VoiceOver conformance.
Direct real-device ergonomics, input/keyboard, latency, interruption and recovery observation.
Visual captures of empty results, open filter/menu controls, long datasets, and Chinese dark AX5; the input reports some relevant tests but the ten frozen PNGs do not show those states.
Observed recruiter first-use comprehension or field usefulness.
